title: Point blowup lowers intersection multiplicity of regular curves
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme and let $Y,Z\subseteq X$ be closed subschemes. Suppose $Y$ is integral of dimension $1$, $p\in Y\cap Z$ is closed, $\mathcal O_{Y,p}$ is regular, and the generic point of $Y$ is not in $Z$. Define $m_p(Y,Z)=\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,p}}(\mathcal O_{Y\cap Z,p})$, with scheme-theoretic intersection cut out by the sum of the ideals. This is a positive finite integer. Blow up $p$, writing $Y',Z'$ for strict transforms and $E$ for the exceptional divisor. Then $Y'\to Y$ is an isomorphism; $Y'\cap E$ consists of a single point $q$, with $m_q(Y',E)=1$; and if $q\in Z'$, then $m_q(Y',Z')<m_p(Y,Z)$. Conventions: [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-sc-generic-point], [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-nagata-strict-transform], [def-weil-pbc-module-length].
